ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all natural persons with 25% or more direct or indirect ownership, directors, authorized signatories, and beneficial owners against the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, the U.S. OFAC SDN list, the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit and Financial Supervisory Service enforcement lists, and Korean domestic criminal and administrative sanctions databases. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons, using the Korean FIU PEP expectations and FATF standards. Continuous transaction monitoring, name-algorithm matching, negative-news screening, and periodic re-screening at every corporate event or share transfer must be performed and documented.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: i-REG Internet Registration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea, Commercial Registration Search System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Korean Commercial Act, a Yuhan Hoesa trade name must be written in Hangul. Roman letters and Arabic numerals may appear only where permitted and must be paired with transliteration in the registration extract. The name must follow the four-tier convention: (1) distinguishing trade name element, (2) business-object statement, (3) legal form indicator 'Yuhan Hoesa', and (4) jurisdictional registration number. Transliterated foreign words must faithfully match the Hangul phonetic rendering, and alternative spellings are deemed different names for registry search purposes.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects the proposed trade name, the applicant must provide a written rejection reason and may appeal under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act to the District Court that supervises the company registry. The appeal petition must be filed within 14 days of service, attaching the rejection notice, the rejected name, the proposed business object, and evidence of no identical or confusingly similar prior registration. Where the rejection is based on a data-entry error in the electronic filing, a correction request to the i-REG registry supervisor should also be filed. If no ministerial approval can succeed for a sensitive token, the applicant should prepare a compliant substitute Hangul trade name while preserving the foreign brand transliteration. A formal legal opinion on the appeal strengths is recommended before filing court objections, and external counsel should preserve all procedural deadlines in writing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Yuhan Hoesa must maintain a registered office in the Republic of Korea for service of process, tax registration, and correspondence from the National Tax Service, municipal authority, and Financial Services Commission. A virtual office or commercial mailbox may be accepted temporarily by the court registry if a valid service agreement exists, but Korean banks and the National Tax Service generally reject a purely virtual address for corporate account opening, VAT registration, invoice issuance, and payroll compliance. For the target email newsletter infrastructure business, a virtual office alone is not recommended; the company should secure a physical office or a regulated business-substance center with dedicated desk space, local director access, lease documentation, and utility records from day one to prevent account refusals and tax registration delays.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspections: registered office signage, physical presence during business hours, lease or ownership documents, original utility bills, employees or responsible director present, corporate documents, accounting records, and business-themed equipment or servers. Quantified risk for a low-risk email infrastructure SaaS company with a physical office is Low-Medium, approximately 15-20% in the first 12 months. Where a virtual office is relied on without local employees or supporting lease evidence, the inspection risk rises to 35-45% and may trigger administrative summons, added corporate audits, or revocation of the business registration.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: The Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 287 to 287-50 (Limited Liability Company, Yuhan Hoesa); the Commercial Registration Act (Act No. 12385, as amended); the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Value-Added Tax Act for business registration; and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act for any reportable foreign shareholding or capital remittance.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registry Division of the Local District Court Registry Office with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office address of the company, administered by the National Court Administration of the Supreme Court of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa), including the executed Articles of Incorporation, subscription and contribution schedule, member identification documents, name-reservation certificate, and all statutory attachments required by the Commercial Registration Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Korean commercial law imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa and no blocked escrow account requirement. The total capital and per-member contributions are freely determined in the Articles of Incorporation. If capital is actually subscribed, each member must pay the full amount of the contribution by the payment date stated in the Articles; if later registered as a foreign-invested company, the foreign member's funds must enter Korea through a licensed foreign exchange bank and be receipted before the foreign-investment report is issued, but this is not an incorporation escrow requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT OF THE MEMBERS AND THE ACTING FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF KR YUHANGHOESA, A YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA.
1. Incorporation and Capital Subscription. RESOLVED, that the Company is duly incorporated as a Yuhan Hoesa under the laws of the Republic of Korea, with the corporate name, business purpose, registered office, financial year, and governance provisions set forth in the Articles of Incorporation. The total subscribed capital of the Company and the amount subscribed by each member are approved exactly as shown in the Articles. The Representative Director is authorized and directed to receive all contribution payments, issue contribution payment receipts, and, where requested, obtain a deposit confirmation certificate from a licensed Korean bank.
2. Banking Authorization. RESOLVED, that the Company will open and maintain one or more corporate bank accounts at a licensed commercial or foreign-exchange bank designated by the Representative Director, for the purpose of receiving operating revenues, including Stripe Billing and credit-card settlement proceeds for the Company's transactional email and newsletter hosting platform. The Representative Director, acting alone or jointly with another officer designated by the Representative Director, is authorized to execute account applications, sign deposit account agreements, approve AML/CFT and KYC certification documents, issue wire-transfer instructions, and close or change signatory authorities when lawfully required.
3. Registered Office. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is adopted as the address set forth in the Articles of Incorporation. The Representative Director and the Company Secretary are jointly instructed to file the registered-office address with the Local District Court Registry Office, the National Tax Service, and, if applicable, the local municipal authority, and to execute lease agreements, virtual-office agreements, or registered-agent arrangements necessary to maintain the registered office.
4. Statutory Officer Appointments. RESOLVED, that the following officers are appointed effective as of the date of these resolutions: a Representative Director with full corporate-management authority; a Director of Compliance and Data Protection responsible for Korea's Personal Information Protection Act regime, anti-spam and newsletter sender disclosure, and privacy policy implementation; and a Company Secretary responsible for statutory registers, corporate filings, and records maintenance. Each officer shall hold office until the next members' meeting or until a successor is duly appointed.
5. Delegation and Indemnification. RESOLVED, that all powers necessary to complete incorporation registration, obtain business registration with the National Tax Service, open bank accounts, make regulatory filings, and engage service providers for electronic payment processing are delegated to the officers. The Company shall indemnify and hold harmless each director and officer to the maximum extent permitted by Korean law for actions taken in good faith in the discharge of duties. All lawful actions taken by the incorporators and officers before the date of these resolutions in connection with the formation of the Company are hereby ratified, confirmed, and approved.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic corporate and VAT administration portal: HomeTax System (hometax.go.kr). Customs export declarations are lodged through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS portal (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the KR_YUHANGHOESA limited liability company (Yuhan Hoesa), a resident corporation is deemed registered by filing an Application for Business Registration with the district tax office (or the HomeTax System) having jurisdiction over its principal domestic place of business within 20 days after business commencement. For a foreign non-resident entity that has no domestic place of business but is liable for value-added tax (e.g., supplying electronic services to Korean non-registrants), the foreign entity must appoint a tax representative in Korea and complete simplified foreign business registration with the National Tax Service through HomeTax; the NTS then issues a Korean Tax Identification Number (TIN, also used as the VAT registration number). Non-resident entities acquiring a domestic permanent establishment must obtain the corporate registration number and business registration certificate under the same procedure as resident companies. There is no minimum capital condition.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic corporation under the Korean Commercial Act and Corporate Tax Act; it is subject to corporate tax at the entity level on worldwide income. It is not eligible for pass-through treatment. A foreign entity without a domestic place of business is taxed only on Korean-source income; the presence of a place of business or an included service supply may create a permanent establishment and expanded registration obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean corporate law and tax law do not provide check-the-box or hybrid mismatch entity-classification elections for domestic Yuhan Hoesa companies. For cross-border structures, Korea applies statutory anti-avoidance rules under the Framework Act on Taxes and the Corporate Tax Act to reclassify transactions that lack economic substance, but no elective pass-through classification is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No KRW turnover threshold for VAT registration. All business operators, including foreign suppliers of electronic services with no Korean place of business, must register for VAT before commencing taxable activities in Korea. A simplified taxable status (reduced relief, not exemption) is available for individuals with annual revenue below KRW 80,000,000, but registration is still mandatory. A foreign electronic service supplier is not exempt based on volume below threshold; registration is required for any supply of qualifying electronic services to Korean non-taxable persons.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoices (e-Tax invoice) must be issued for all B2B VAT supplies and transmitted to the NTS HomeTax system by the day following the supply date. There is no real-time fiscal clearance, government-certified digital stamping, or customs API clearance for normal VAT invoices in Korea. Export declarations are cleared separately via the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system. Large taxpayers may use API/EDI integration with HomeTax for e-invoice submission, but validation is not a pre-supply clearance condition.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Korean VAT Act, exported goods are zero-rated upon the export declaration to Korean customs. Services, including the bulk transactional email API, email newsletter hosting infrastructure and associated SaaS data processing services, qualify for 0% VAT when exported to non-residents, provided (i) the contract is made with a non-resident counterparty, (ii) the consideration is conclusively received in foreign currency through a Korean foreign exchange bank, and (iii) the service is actually performed or used outside Korea or is provided for the non-resident's use outside Korea. Intra-company overseas service transactions also require documentary evidence of the actual overseas provision.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration submitted via UNI-PASS for any physical goods components
Air Waybill or Bill of Lading evidencing cross-border movement (goods only)
Commercial invoice and zero-rated tax invoice referencing the export contract
Foreign Exchange Bank Purchase Confirmation or Inward Remittance Confirmation evidencing receipt of foreign currency
Export contract or service order stipulating the non-resident customer and foreign-currency consideration
Evidence of offshore service consumption (e.g., customer performance logs, infrastructure usage records supplied to overseas principal)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service audits zero-rated export claims on a transaction-by-transaction basis, requiring the exporter or service provider to retain and produce the full documentation bundle. If foreign exchange is repatriated after the prescribed deadline or the overseas-use/foreign-customer conditions are not substantiated, the NTS will disallow the 0% rate, assess VAT at 10% on the full consideration, and impose additional tax. False or fraudulent zero-rating claims, including tax invoice forgery and fake export documentation, can trigger criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and penalty taxes under the VAT Act, with additional tax rates commonly ranging from 20% to 40% of the underpaid VAT, depending on intent, plus any customs penalties if the export declaration was falsified.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the principal foreign exchange policy authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; the Korea Customs Service supervises cross-border currency and goods movement at frontier points.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberal but regulated foreign exchange regime. Current account transactions under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act are broadly convertible, meaning the Yuhan Hoesa can receive Stripe settlement proceeds, pay overseas cloud infrastructure vendors, license software, remit royalties, and repatriate after-tax dividends through a designated foreign exchange bank without a blanket prior approval, provided each transaction is correctly classified and reported through the electronic foreign exchange information system. Capital account transactions are less automatic: any non-resident equity injection into the Korean LLC must be declared as foreign direct investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act through the bank or KOTRA, and any outward capital transaction such as a foreign-currency loan, guarantee, or material equity investment requires a separate report or approval threshold assessment. The KRW is managed floating and is not subject to an in-country surrender requirement for export proceeds, but every inward and outward remittance must carry a valid MOEF Foreign Exchange Transaction purpose code. Profit remittance is ultimately allowable for a Yuhan Hoesa if accumulated retained earnings are supported by audited tax and financial statements, a board resolution declares the dividend, the Foreign Investment Company registration or FDI notification is current, and the shareholder loan account for capital remittance is in order. In practice the major operational hurdles are document-intensive bank underwriting, stringent beneficial ownership verification for non-resident shareholders, and the bank’s internal requirement that software-subscription revenue models show genuine recurring business contracts rather than ambiguous cross-border collections.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For services and software-based export proceeds such as email newsletter infrastructure subscriptions, the exporter is required to collect and deposit the foreign currency consideration inside a domestic foreign exchange bank account within the statutory collection period prescribed by the MOEF, generally aligned with the contractual settlement date and not exceeding five years for meritorious trade receivables under standard export claims. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; the mandatory surrender ratio is effectively 0%, meaning the company may retain USD or other foreign currency proceeds in a foreign currency account, exchange them into KRW at the prevailing market rate, or use them directly for permissible foreign-currency disbursements. All export receipts, including those received through global payment intermediaries such as Stripe, must ultimately be booked through a Korean designated foreign exchange bank and reported with the correct BOK/MOEF export-revenue purpose classification; extension of the settlement timeline beyond statutory limits requires a documentary evidentiary submission for bank or MOEF approval.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMI viability is low and effectively non-feasible for a Korean-resident corporate entity. An offshore digital EMI without a licensed Korean branch cannot lawfully issue KRW-denominated resident corporate accounts, accept deposits, or execute onshore foreign exchange transactions under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Korean Electronic Financial Transactions Act. Only domestic tier-1 commercial banks licensed as foreign exchange banks can legally hold capital escrow accounts, operational currency accounts, and cross-border clearing mandates for the Yuhan Hoesa.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean top-tier banks require at least one statutory director, ultimate beneficial owner, or an approved Korea-resident authorized signatory to appear physically at the corporate banking branch for the initial KYC interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not uniformly accepted; some banks permit a power of attorney that is notarized, apostilled, and accompanied by certified passport copies, but most tier-1 bank compliance committees insist on an in-branch principal identity check or a recorded video interview with the actual signatory. The safest treasury blueprint is to appoint a Korean-resident responsible director or legal representative with branch attendance capability.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders with layered holding structures and no clear natural-person ultimate beneficial owner, especially if nominee entities, trusts, or low-disclosure jurisdictions obscure ownership above the 25% threshold.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete group organizational chart down to each natural person holding more than 10% of the equity; certified passport copies and foreign ID for each ultimate beneficial owner; apostilled or consular-certified UBO declaration using the bank FATF style form; certified certificate of incorporation and good-standing certificates for every holding vehicle; certified bank reference letters and three months of source-of-funds bank statements for investors; clean-source-of-wealth declaration signed by each shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicious inbound payment velocity from Stripe and credit-card settlement flows that do not reconcile with the stated email-newsletter SaaS subscription model, causing possible active money-laundering trend detection or unauthorized payment aggregation concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed merchant-of-record agreement with the payment processor; live demonstration or technical architecture documentation of the bulk transactional email API platform; detailed subscriber consent and opt-in management dashboard records; anti-spam compliance certification and DMARC/SPF/DKIM authentication evidence; three years of audited financial statements and trial balance; cycle-accurate invoice, payment receipt, and transaction ledger mapping to the BOK foreign-currency export classification; board-resolution-approved operating revenue forecast; company data-protection and privacy registration under PIPA/PIPC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Global newsletter subscriber base and marketing data infrastructure creating sanctions, PEP, and adverse-media exposure, particularly if subscriber lists, client domains, or IP geolocations touch comprehensively embargoed jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written AML/CFT sanctions-screening and watchlist policy with audit trails; contractual prohibition on serving embargoed-jurisdiction end customers; intellectual property, trademark, and domain ownership record; domain reputation and email-sending IP history; country geo-blocking and consent audit logs; PIPC data-processing registration; external legal opinion confirming the SaaS platform is not equated to a payment service or remittance service; evidence of no prior PEP or sanctioned-party screening hits and a commitment to notify the bank within 24 hours of any adverse-media development.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance and registered-address mismatch when the Yuhan Hoesa uses a virtual office or registered agent address without employees, physical operating presence, or a designated Korean compliance officer for FX and AML obligations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial lease agreement or serviced-office agreement in the company’s name; Korean business registration certificate; payroll records and income-tax payment slips for at least one Korea-resident responsible employee or director; corporate resolution appointing an AML/FX compliance officer; annual operating budget and cash-flow plan; data-center, email relay, or hosting vendor contracts proving real infrastructure operation; confirmation that no nominee director is engaged and that day-to-day management is transparent and locatable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident capital injection must be routed through a properly filed Foreign Direct Investment notification under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act at a designated domestic foreign exchange bank. The overseas shareholder remits funds from its own bank account, never from an anonymous or third-party pool, via SWIFT MT103, with a clear BKEF or MOEF foreign exchange purpose code matching a non-resident share subscription in a Korean direct-investment target. The bank will book the inward remittance into a temporary foreign-currency settlement account, convert it into KRW when appropriate, and credit a capital escrow account pending issuance of the share capital. The company must then obtain a capital verification certificate from an eligible Korean external auditor or certified public accountant confirming that the paid-in amount matches the subscribed share capital, after which the bank treats the capital as verified and available for treasury deployment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational trade disbursements for the email newsletter infrastructure include cloud hosting, email API provider fees, SMS delivery, software licensing, consulting, and other cross-border service costs; these are cleared via SWIFT MT103 remittances through a designated Korean foreign exchange bank, with each outward payment carrying the appropriate remittance purpose code and an underlying invoice or service agreement. For physical hardware purchases such as servers, network devices, or data-center equipment, an irrevocable letter of credit, either at sight or by usance, is the preferred clearing rail when the vendor requires transactional payment protection. Documentary collections D/P and D/A remain available for smaller-value or relationship-based physical trade settlements supported by clean transport documents, invoices, and insurance certificates; all outbound trade flows must be reconciled against the statutory FX notification thresholds and the foreign-currency account transaction history to maintain audit-ready compliance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD forward exchange contracts backed by genuine current or capital account exposure with an underlying invoice, subscription receipt, or dividend obligation
FX swaps between KRW and USD for liquidity timing and working-capital management within the bank’s approved derivative limit
Cross-currency swaps matching fixed or floating USD funding against KRW revenue when a sustainable underlying exposure is documented

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) structures executed through a licensed domestic foreign exchange bank or an approved offshore NDF counterparty for hedging KRW trade and investment positions where physical delivery is impractical

Currency options and option combinations such as collars or participating forwards, only when the board approves the derivative policy, the bank confirms real-demand eligibility, and the instrument is not speculative

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and annual report (Saupbogoseo) filing for a Yuhan Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal year ending December 31, the corporate income tax return must be filed by March 31 of the following year. A one-month extension to April 30 is available if the financial statements are approved at the annual shareholders' meeting by the original due date. No separate commercial registry annual renewal filing is required for a Yuhan Hoesa; the annual report data is submitted with the tax return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing of the corporate income tax return triggers a 20% penalty on the underreported or unpaid tax, plus an additional daily surcharge of 0.022% on unpaid tax from the day after the due date until paid (capped at approximately 9.3% of the unpaid amount). Continued default may lead to enforced collection, asset seizure, criminal tax evasion referral, and administrative strike-off by the commercial registry for dormancy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local income tax surcharge (Jibangsosde) payment and return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government tax authority / National Tax Service (collected jointly with the national corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the national corporate income tax return: March 31 (or April 30 with extension) for a December 31 fiscal year-end entity.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues the same 0.022% daily surcharge on unpaid local income tax. Non-payment may trigger enforced collection through the local government's tax seizure and collection procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting and approval of financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate governance requirement under the Korean Commercial Act; no separate government filing unless a change is registered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must hold within 3 months after each fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, by March 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the annual shareholders' meeting or to prepare financial statements may result in administrative fines of up to KRW 2,000,000 (approximately USD 1,500) per non-complying director. It may also constitute grounds for director disqualification and adversely affect the company's good standing with regulators.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial registry maintenance and change reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korean Commercial Registry (Court of Registry, Ministry of Court Administration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No separate annual renewal exists; however, any change in registered office, director, shareholder, or authorized capital must be filed within 2 weeks (14 days) of the occurrence.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to register changes may incur a non-compliance penalty (Kwajanggeum) of up to KRW 2,000,000 (approximately USD 1,500) per infraction. An entity that fails to maintain a valid registered address or file statutory returns may face administrative strike-off through dormancy procedures after public notice, resulting in loss of legal personality.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership information confirmation and 30-day change reporting under the Financial Transaction Reports Act (UBO regime)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) through the company's compliance officer / registered agent; no public UBO register in South Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once per fiscal year, the company must confirm the identity and holdings of every ultimate beneficial owner (holding 25% or more capital or control). Any share transfer or change in ownership resulting in a UBO change must be reported to the designated compliance officer and recorded within 30 days of the transaction.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report UBO information or providing false data may result in administrative fines up to KRW 30,000,000 (approximately USD 22,000) for serious violations, and criminal penalties (imprisonment or fine) for intentional concealment of beneficial ownership.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its delegated rules, a Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily required to undergo an external audit by a licensed CPA firm if it meets any of the following quantitative thresholds at the fiscal year-end: (a) total assets exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9,000,000); (b) total revenue exceeds KRW 10,000,000,000 (approximately USD 7,500,000); (c) average number of regular employees exceeds 300; or (d) the entity is a public company, financial company, or otherwise designated by the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS). A voluntary audit or review is additionally required by certain banks, investors, or tax authorities when seeking credit or tax-exemption certifications. For entities below the statutory threshold, an audit may still be required under industry-specific rules if the entity provides enterprise-grade infrastructure services to regulated customers.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for listed companies and designated large entities; Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (Korean GAAP) for non-listed small and medium-sized companies. Simplified accounting standards for micro-entities may be applied if the company is below the above thresholds. The audit must adhere to the Korean Standards on Auditing (KSA) issued by the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA) and FSS regulatory directives.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a public UBO register; instead, every corporation must maintain an internal beneficial ownership register under the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information. The designated compliance officer or registered agent must verify and confirm the identities of all ultimate beneficial owners owning or controlling 25% or more of shares or voting rights at least once per fiscal year. Any share transfer or ownership change that alters a UBO must be reported in writing within 30 days of the transaction and recorded in the corporate books. The register must be made available to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) upon lawful demand. The company must annually obtain written confirmation from each UBO, and failure to do so may subject the company and the non-compliant UBO to fines.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders' and Directors' Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 15,000 for a licensed CPA audit of a non-listed Korean LLC, depending on asset size, transaction volume, and complexity of email infrastructure revenue recognition; USD 3,000 - USD 8,000 for a voluntary review below the statutory audit threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal corporate income tax rate on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion; progressive lower brackets apply below that threshold
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The Korean Corporate Income Tax Act and the Special Tax Reduction Control Act grant R&D credits, foreign-invested enterprise tax holidays in Free Economic Zones, and various employment-related credits; there is no standalone patent box, but qualifying technology/royalty income may benefit from deduction mechanisms; a 10% local income tax surcharge applies on the national corporate income tax payable; losses may be carried forward for 15 years for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2020

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 1101) filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, supplemented by interim advance corporate income tax payments during the fiscal year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the close of the taxable year; for a calendar-year taxpayer, no later than March 31 of the following year; for a Korean foreign-invested company with an approved non-calendar fiscal year, by the last day of the third month following that fiscal year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Corporate Identity and Business Year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Records taxpayer registration number, legal name, representative director, business year, and whether the entity is a domestic or foreign corporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that Yuhan Hoesa is a Korean domestic corporation taxed on worldwide income; provide the Korean registration number; disclose the foreign shareholder's name, country of residence, and tax identification number in the shareholder disclosure schedule; identify any non-resident ultimate beneficial owner for transparency and CFC review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computes gross income, deductible expenses, non-deductible items, and the final taxable income before tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all Korean-source income and expenses; do not deduct management fees, royalties, or intercompany service charges to foreign related parties unless supported by arm's-length contracts, actual service evidence, and transfer pricing documentation; foreign-exchange and intercompany accruals should be corrected to avoid a distorted tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 7 - Transfer Pricing and Controlled Transactions Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reports all cross-border transactions with foreign related parties, including the transaction type, amount, applied pricing method, and documentary references.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If cross-border controlled transactions exceed KRW 10 billion in the fiscal year, attach the Local File; if annual revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion and controlled transactions exceed KRW 5 billion, attach the Master File; the non-resident parent should provide its tax residency certificate and intercompany agreements for the email newsletter infrastructure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculates the foreign income tax credit for corporate income taxes paid by the Korean company on foreign-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach evidence of foreign tax payment and the tax return of the foreign PE or foreign-source income; the foreign tax credit is limited to the aggregate Korean tax on that foreign-source income; do not claim a foreign tax credit for taxes borne by the non-resident shareholder on an outbound dividend.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 12 - Withholding on Payments to Non-Residents
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reports dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-resident corporations or individuals and the Korean withholding tax collected and remitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For every outbound dividend, interest, and royalty payment, complete the payee schedule showing country of residence, tax residency certificate, beneficial ownership status, treaty article relied on, and treaty withholding rate; if no treaty relief is claimed, apply the statutory non-resident WHT of 22% (20% national plus 2% local income tax surcharge).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 14 - Advance Payments and Net Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summarizes interim corporate tax payments made during the fiscal year and determines the final balance payable or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean LLC must pay interim advance corporate income tax based on the prior-year amount or estimated current-year income; non-resident shareholders cannot be credited with advances paid by the LLC; make the final payment by the statutory deadline to avoid daily late-payment surcharges.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an additional tax equal to 20% of the unpaid corporate income tax; under-reporting the tax base attracts additional tax of 10% to 40% depending on falsity or the use of fabricated invoices; daily late-payment surcharges accrue under the Framework Act on National Taxes until full payment; fraudulent returns are referred for criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and may lead to imprisonment and fines computed on the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge) for non-resident corporate shareholders absent an applicable tax treaty; treaty-reduced rates may apply if the shareholder is the beneficial owner and qualifies for relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The withholding agent must file the non-resident tax treaty exemption/reduction application with the National Tax Service through HomeTax before or at the time of payment, attaching the Tax Residency Certificate issued by the treaty jurisdiction, a beneficial ownership declaration and supporting analysis, shareholding and holding-period evidence for dividend relief, and intercompany agreements proving no conduit or pass-through arrangements; if withholding was already made, the non-resident must file a refund claim with the District Tax Office, generally within three years; treaty relief is denied where the recipient is not the beneficial owner or where the principal purpose of the arrangement is treaty shopping.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory non-treaty withholding on cross-border royalties and intercompany interest is 22% (20% national plus 2% local); under Korea's OECD-based double tax treaties, interest is often reduced to 10% and royalties to 10-15%, with some older treaties preserving 15% or 20% rates; royalties paid for the use of software, algorithms, or email infrastructure IP are scrutinized against arm's-length value and economic substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is required when aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 10 billion for the fiscal year; Master File is required when annual revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion and cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 5 billion; documentation must be submitted with the corporate income tax return and the National Tax Service may request contemporaneous evidence regardless of threshold in an audit.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply a separate Economic Substance Regulation code, but the substance-over-form principle, the beneficial ownership requirement in tax treaty relief, the general anti-avoidance rule under Article 5 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, and controlled foreign company rules require real Korean economic activities; for the email newsletter infrastructure, core income-generating activities such as server hosting, client contracting, data processing, personnel management, and call support must be performed by the Korean LLC and cannot be artificially shifted to an offshore shell with no operational capacity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Corporate Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a Corporate Income Tax Return that deliberately omits revenue from email newsletter subscriptions, inflates intercompany expenses, or uses fabricated invoices to reduce taxable income with intent to evade Korean corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act; punishment may include imprisonment for a term up to five years, or a fine, or both, with aggravated penalties when the evaded tax amount exceeds the statutory criminal threshold; the National Tax Service also imposes additional tax of up to 40% of the understated tax and late-payment surcharges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil: directors who knowingly sign or submit fraudulent returns may be held jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax, penalties, and civil restitution; the court may order asset seizure and overseas travel blacklisting under the National Tax Collection Act; criminal imprisonment terms apply if the director directed or benefited from the fraudulent scheme.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into non-arm's-length transactions with foreign related parties, such as overpriced software licensing, management charges, or email infrastructure fees, while the Korean LLC lacks sufficient personnel, premises, server assets, and risk-bearing capacity; failing to prepare and submit the required Local File and Master File.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Articles 5 and 6 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs permit the National Tax Service to re-determine the taxable income as if the transactions had occurred at arm's length; related adjustments are subject to penalty taxes, additional tax for under-reporting, and daily late-payment surcharges; criminal prosecution can follow if the taxpayer uses fabricated transfer pricing documents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil: directors who authorized the artificial pricing structure may be personally liable when corporate assets are insufficient to pay the tax assessment under Article 39 of the Framework Act on National Taxes; they face civil damages for breach of fiduciary duty, travel blacklisting, and imprisonment if the pricing scheme is shown to be a fraudulent tax evasion mechanism.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax / DTA and Shell Dividend Stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, or royalties to a non-resient parent or conduit company without withholding the statutory 22% WHT, or claiming treaty-reduced withholding rates using a shell intermediary that lacks substantive economic activity and is not the beneficial owner of the income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 98 of the Corporate Income Tax Act imposes the 22% statutory withholding obligation on Korean payers; under the Framework Act on National Taxes, the failed withholding agent is liable for the uncollected tax, negligence penalties, and daily late-payment surcharges; the National Tax Service may deny treaty benefits under the beneficial ownership and principal purpose tests and impose additional corporate income tax, penalties, and criminal sanctions for wilful non-collection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil: directors who cause the Korean LLC to withhold nothing and remit the full amount offshore are personally liable for the withheld taxes and related interest; personal assets can be seized and an overseas travel ban imposed; criminal imprisonment is possible under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act where the payment structure was designed to defeat Korean tax collection.
